title: The Four Last Things: Death and Judgment
summary: Death and Judgment are the first two of the Four Last Things, reminding us that life is a pilgrimage toward eternity; at death, each soul faces particular judgment and receives its eternal destiny—Heaven, Purgatory, or Hell—based on its response to God's grace.

blocks.text: Introduction: The Four Last Things

The Four Last Things—Death, Judgment, Heaven, and Hell—are traditional themes of Christian meditation and preaching. They remind us of the ultimate realities that await every person and call us to live each day in preparation for eternity. Meditating on these truths helps us to detach from worldly things and to seek first the Kingdom of God. [CCC 1006-1007]

Death is the end of man's earthly pilgrimage, of the time of grace and mercy which God offers him to work out his earthly life in conformity with the divine plan and to decide his ultimate destiny. Judgment follows death, when each person receives retribution in his immortal soul at the very moment of death in a particular judgment that refers his life to Christ. [CCC 1013, 1021-1022]
And just as it is appointed for men to die once, and after that comes judgment.

blocks.title: CCC 1006-1007: Ultimate Realities
blocks.text: The Four Last Things remind us of the ultimate realities awaiting every person; meditating on them helps us detach from worldly things and seek first the Kingdom of God.
I. The Reality of Death

Death is the separation of the soul from the body. The human person, created as a unity of body and soul, experiences death as the dissolution of this unity. Yet the soul does not perish; it survives the body and awaits reunion with it at the resurrection. [CCC 1005, 1016]

Death is a consequence of sin. Although man's nature is mortal, God had destined him not to die. Death entered the world as a consequence of Adam's sin, but Christ transformed death by his own death and Resurrection, turning it from a punishment into a passage to eternal life. [CCC 1008, 1019]
Therefore as sin came into the world through one man and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because all men sinned.

blocks.title: CCC 1005: Separation of Soul and Body
blocks.text: Death is the separation of soul from body; the soul survives and awaits reunion with the body at the resurrection, transformed by Christ's death and Resurrection.
II. Death Transformed by Christ

Christ looked upon death with serenity because he trusted in his Father's love. By his obedience unto death, Jesus transformed the curse of death into a blessing. For Christians, to die is to be with Christ, which is far better than remaining in this world. [CCC 1010-1011]

Through Christ, death can become an act of love and obedience to the Father. By dying in Christ, we die in God's grace, freed from sin and ready to enter eternal life. The Christian can say with St. Paul: For me to live is Christ, and to die is gain. [CCC 1014, 1020]

For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain. If it is to be life in the flesh, that means fruitful labor for me. Yet which I shall choose I cannot tell. I am hard pressed between the two. My desire is to depart and be with Christ, for that is far better.

blocks.title: CCC 1010-1011: Death Transformed
blocks.text: By his obedience unto death, Christ transformed the curse of death into a blessing; for Christians, to die is to be with Christ, which is far better.
III. Preparing for a Holy Death

We must prepare for death throughout our lives, living each day in God's grace and friendship. The Church prays for a happy death in the Litany of the Saints: From sudden and unprovided death, deliver us, O Lord. A holy death is the culmination of a life lived in union with Christ. [CCC 1014]

The sacraments, especially Penance and the Anointing of the Sick, prepare us for death. Viaticum, the Eucharist received at the approach of death, is the seed of eternal life and the power of resurrection. Prayer, almsgiving, and works of mercy also help us to die in God's grace. [CCC 1020, 1523-1525]
Therefore you also must be ready; for the Son of man is coming at an hour you do not expect.

blocks.title: CCC 1014: Prepare for Death
blocks.text: We must prepare for death by living each day in God's grace; the sacraments, especially Penance and Anointing of the Sick, and Viaticum prepare us for a holy death.
IV. The Particular Judgment

Each man receives his eternal retribution in his immortal soul at the very moment of his death, in a particular judgment that refers his life to Christ. This judgment determines whether the soul enters immediately into the blessedness of Heaven, undergoes purification in Purgatory, or is condemned to eternal separation from God in Hell. [CCC 1022]

The particular judgment is the fulfillment of God's justice and mercy. God judges each person according to his works and the disposition of his heart. No one can escape this judgment, and it reveals the truth about each life lived in the light of Christ. [CCC 1021, 1039]
For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive good or evil, according to what he has done in the body.

blocks.title: CCC 1022: Particular Judgment
blocks.text: At death, each soul receives eternal retribution in a particular judgment, entering Heaven, undergoing purification in Purgatory, or being condemned to Hell based on life in Christ.
V. The Final Judgment

The Last Judgment will come when Christ returns in glory at the end of time. Then all the dead will be raised, and Christ will pronounce the final word on all history and on every human life. The Last Judgment will reveal the ultimate meaning of God's work of creation and redemption. [CCC 1038-1039]

The Last Judgment will manifest God's justice and mercy before all creation. It will reveal the good and evil deeds of every person and the consequences of each action. This judgment will bring to completion the particular judgment and establish the definitive order of the Kingdom of God. [CCC 1039-1041]

When the Son of man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne. Before him will be gathered all the nations, and he will separate them one from another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.

blocks.title: CCC 1038-1039: Last Judgment
blocks.text: The Last Judgment will come when Christ returns in glory; all will be raised, and Christ will pronounce the final word on history and every human life, revealing God's justice and mercy.
VI. Heaven: The Fulfillment of Hope

Heaven is the ultimate end and fulfillment of the deepest human longings, the state of supreme and definitive happiness. Those who die in God's grace and friendship and are perfectly purified live forever with Christ, seeing God face to face as he is. This is the beatific vision, the fullness of life and love. [CCC 1023-1026]

In Heaven, we shall be perfectly united with the Blessed Trinity and with all the saints. There will be no more death, mourning, crying, or pain, for the former things have passed away. Heaven is not a place but a state of eternal communion with God, the source of all joy. [CCC 1026-1027, 1045]
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning nor crying nor pain any more, for the former things have passed away.

blocks.title: CCC 1023-1026: Beatific Vision
blocks.text: Heaven is supreme happiness, where those purified see God face to face in the beatific vision, perfectly united with the Trinity and all the saints in eternal communion.
VII. Purgatory: Purification After Death

Purgatory is the state of those who die in God's friendship but still need purification before entering Heaven. They are assured of eternal salvation, but they undergo purification to achieve the holiness necessary to enter the joy of Heaven. The Church prays for the souls in Purgatory and offers Masses for their repose. [CCC 1030-1032]

The doctrine of Purgatory is based on the practice of praying for the dead and on Scripture's reference to a purification after death. This purification is not a second chance but the completion of sanctification begun on earth. The prayers and sacrifices of the living can help the souls in Purgatory. [CCC 1032]
Thus he made atonement for the dead that they might be delivered from their sin.

blocks.title: CCC 1030-1032: Purification
blocks.text: Purgatory is the state of those who die in God's friendship but need purification before Heaven; they are assured of salvation and aided by the prayers of the living.
VIII. Hell: Eternal Separation from God

Hell is the state of definitive self-exclusion from communion with God and the blessed. It is the consequence of dying in mortal sin without repentance. God does not predestine anyone to Hell; it is the result of a person's free and persistent rejection of God's love and grace. [CCC 1033-1035]

The chief punishment of Hell is eternal separation from God, in whom alone man can possess the life and happiness for which he was created. The Church affirms the reality of Hell and calls us to conversion, warning us against presumption and despair. God desires all to be saved, but respects human freedom. [CCC 1035, 1037]
Then he will say to those at his left hand, Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.

blocks.title: CCC 1033-1035: Self-Exclusion
blocks.text: Hell is definitive self-exclusion from God, the consequence of dying in mortal sin without repentance; God does not predestine anyone to Hell but respects human freedom.
IX. Living in Light of Eternity

The Church encourages us to meditate on the Four Last Things to live wisely and faithfully. Remembering death and judgment helps us to use our time well, to avoid sin, and to grow in virtue. The hope of Heaven and the fear of Hell motivate us to persevere in God's grace. [CCC 1007, 1014]

We must live each day as if it were our last, ready to meet the Lord at any moment. Regular examination of conscience, frequent confession, and devotion to the Eucharist keep us prepared. The saints lived with eternity in view, and their example inspires us to do the same. [CCC 1014, 1470]

Therefore gird up your minds, be sober, set your hope fully upon the grace that is coming to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ. As obedient children, do not be conformed to the passions of your former ignorance.

blocks.title: CCC 1007: Meditate on Eternity
blocks.text: Meditating on the Four Last Things helps us live wisely, avoid sin, and grow in virtue; we must live each day ready to meet the Lord at any moment.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer: Prayer for a Happy Death
blocks.text: O Lord God, remember not my sins when you come to judge me. Grant me the grace to die in your friendship, purified by your mercy. May I be found worthy to enter your Kingdom, where there is no death or sorrow, but life everlasting. Through the intercession of the Blessed Virgin Mary and all the saints, hear my prayer. Amen.
